_source: House style: edit here, both runtimes follow. v1.0.7 (2026-09-11, mycelium gate-research Day 20, F1020 s.4, queen dispatch 2026-09-11T123500Z-1103): OpenAI published its own GPT-6 Astra model-guidance page (2026-09-05) naming a producer-side slop-word/stock-phrase blocklist; checked against the live catalog (not from memory). Added as HARD phraseTells: 'Bottom Line:'/'In short:' colon-anchored summary openers (sibling of the already-HARD 'in conclusion/in summary' tell, colon-anchored to spare the common connective 'in short supply'-class phrasing); the two-sentence 'This isn't about X. It's about Y.' structural reframe (distinct from the existing intensifier+comma 'not just X, it's/but Y' HARD tell -- no intensifier, no joining punctuation, two full sentences). Added to watchlist (cluster-WARN only, same unlock/seamless/maximize reasoning -- both are common legitimate adverbs, e.g. 'genuinely useful', 'importantly, check the warranty'): bare 'importantly', bare 'genuinely'. Declined after being built and canary-tested: the plain comma-form contrastive 'X, not Y' was implemented as a WARN/density structural counter in engine.js (same shape as the existing notXbutY density counter, on the theory that a single occurrence is ordinary human phrasing like 'tea, not coffee' and only repeated over-use reads as a tell), then run against livingwebsites.ca's own 258 shipped, gate-passed public pages -- 89 (34%) exceeded the density cap, several by a wide margin, showing this is the fleet's own ordinary rhetorical voice, not an AI-specific tell in this corpus; shipping it would be exactly the false-positive-noise-gets-ignored failure mode the mailto/double-hyphen WARN-first precedent exists to avoid, so it was reverted rather than shipped. The em-dash sibling 'X-not Y' needs no new rule regardless, since any em dash already HARD-fails via the existing char tell. Parked, not built: OpenAI's 'Question? Answer.' rhetorical self-Q&A pattern -- too structurally close to a legitimate, load-bearing trades-copywriting hook (rhetorical-question-then-terse-answer) already in real use on this fleet's own shipped pages; building it risks a high false-positive rate against genuine marketing voice, and the source description is too underspecified (no worked example given, unlike every other item on the list) to write a tight pattern against. Also parked: the invented-hyphenated-compound-label detector ('exact-head checks', 'editorial-row layouts') -- not a fixed phrase, would need a structural heuristic (novel adjective-noun hyphenated compound absent from a stopword/known-compound list) that is a materially harder and riskier detector class than anything else in this catalog; no such heuristic exists yet and building one without a corpus of known-good hyphenated compounds (trade terms like 'gutter-guard', 'multi-service') risks a false-positive flood on ordinary compound-noun trades vocabulary. v1.0.1: bare 'unlock' pulled from HARD phraseTells (strong functional sense, e.g. 'unlock this step/account/feature'; over-fired on progressive-disclosure UI microcopy in production, 2026-07-01); stays in watchlist for cluster-WARN. 'elevate'/'seamless' remain HARD (reliably filler as bare words). v1.0.2: added 'in today's <adj> world' (sibling of the fast-paced tell). Held as too functional/common for HARD (unlock precedent): 'a sense of / air of / notion of', 'here's the thing/kicker', bare 'worth noting/mentioning'; elevate/seamless demotion held pending a second consumer signal. v1.0.3: provenance note rewritten for release (internal sourcing references removed); tell definitions unchanged. v1.0.4 (2026-07-23, engine v1.0.6, dispatch 2026-07-23T163600Z-001 + 2026-07-23T171400Z-001): added a spaced/unspaced double-hyphen ('--') structural WARN in engine.js's findStructuralWarnings (NOT a catalog-driven charTells/phraseTells entry, since that group is hard-fail and a fleet blast-radius scan found ~41 already-shipped own-site pages using this em-dash-substitute construction; see engine.js's DOUBLE_HYPHEN_RE comment for the full reasoning). Promoted to hard ERROR on livingwebsites.ca's own served-page gate the same day, after the ~5 real own-site instances found were rewritten to real punctuation. Other tell definitions unchanged. v1.0.5 (2026-07-29, queen dispatch 2026-07-29T223500Z-001, reply to F912's full-pool sweep): 'seamless' narrowed from a bare-word HARD match to a phrase-pattern -- the bare word false-positived on real gutter-guard/eavestrough businesses' own correct product-category term ('seamless gutters'/'seamless eavestrough', 2 real prospects blocked at the voice stage, 2/2 repeatable). The regex now hard-fails 'seamless'/'seamlessly' EXACTLY as before EXCEPT when immediately followed by 'gutter(s)'/'eavestrough(s)'/'trough(s)' (a negative lookahead exclusion, not a positive filler-noun allowlist) -- so every other marketing-filler collocation ('seamless experience', 'seamless integration', 'seamless workflow', and any future uncatalogued filler noun) still hard-fails exactly as before; only the specific real trade-vocabulary collocation is spared. 'elevate' is untouched (still bare-word HARD). Regression fixtures both ways added to this repo's own test/engine.test.js and livingwebsites' test/de-ai.test.js. NOTE: this working-tree edit was made directly (not via a separate feature branch) by the livingwebsites worker per its own dispatch; pending a formal commit + version-tag + re-vendor confirmation (the worker's own fences forbid git commit/push this tick) -- see livingwebsites oversight/results/2026-07-29T223500Z-001.md section 1 for the full before/after regex and both-direction fixture evidence. v1.0.6 (2026-08-23, mycelium gate-research 2026-08-23T073533Z, Findings 1+2, engine v1.0.10): added 'deep dive' and 'maximise'/'maximize' to the watchlist (cluster-WARN only, never HARD) -- both named as overused-AI-writing terms by a 2026-07-30 Economist corpus study (55,940 sentences, its own journalism vs. the same pieces rewritten by ChatGPT/Claude/Gemini/Grok); 'delve' and 'tapestry' from the same study's list are already HARD tells here, corroborating this list targets the same register lw generates in. 'deep dive' is the comma-less sibling of the already-HARD 'let's dive in'. Watchlist tier (not HARD) is deliberate for both, same reasoning as 'unlock'/'seamless': 'maximize attic ventilation' is legitimate functional trades copy, so it only WARNs when it clusters with a second watchlist word in one paragraph. Separately, the SAME study named the plain 'not X but Y' / 'not only ... but also' antithesis (without a comma) as an overused AI rhetorical device; engine.js's findStructuralWarnings notXbutY density counter required a comma before 'but' and missed this comma-less form entirely -- fixed there (not a catalog change) by making the comma optional, tier unchanged (WARN/density, cap 1/400w). The existing HARD phraseTell 'not just X, it's/but Y reframe' (intensifier + comma/em-dash/semicolon required) is UNCHANGED per the research's explicit recommendation -- it stays the aggressive, intensified form.

phraseTells.name: not just X, it's/but Y reframe

this isn't about X, it's about Y (two-sentence reframe)
